content:
As mentioned earlier this year, Google Chrome has now switched to a biweekly release cycle.

Previously, Chrome had a major "milestone" update every four weeks, such as jumping from version 100 to version 101. Before 2021, Google used a six-week cycle.

The switch to major updates every two weeks aims to "deliver new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes more quickly." Each update will contain less content, but will be paired with a higher update frequency.

Google also stated that this "accelerated pace is good for the web as a whole." Developers will be able to "roll out modern web features with greater confidence, because the deployment window is tighter, interoperability updates can be delivered faster, and security improvements can reach users across platforms more quickly." Each "smaller release scope" will also make it "faster to pinpoint regressions."

On the security front, Google said that in the face of threats posed by the rise of artificial intelligence, this change helps "defend against rapidly evolving threats."

For enterprise customers, Chrome offers the "Extended Stable" channel, which updates every eight weeks: Chrome 156 is released first, followed by version 160. Google said most enterprise users should adopt the Stable version, which updates every two weeks.

Chrome 153 is rolling out starting today on desktop, Android, and iOS platforms. Version 154 will be available on September 22.
